title: TRI UK on Twitter
summary: I first worked on TRI UK's Twitter account following my manager's plan. When I took over social, I changed how we tweeted, and the account had the best two years in its history.

facts.label: Client
facts.value: TRI UK, triathlon and cycling retail

main.label: more engagement per tweet in my two years leading social than in the three years before.

others.label: tweets scoring 10 or more, against 10 before

trend.heading: My two years leading social were the account's best
trend.intro: I looked at every tweet from 2014 to 2019 and split them into before and after I led social.

cards.text: 12.6 tweets a month. More than a third were Instagram auto-shares.

cards.measure: engagements per tweet, the account's highest
cards.text: 16.5 tweets a month, almost all with native images.

trend.title: Average engagement per tweet over time
trend.alt: Average engagement per tweet over time. Before I led social: 1.96, 2.65, 1.44, 0.86 and 1.42 from Jul 2014 to Jul 2017. My time: 1.96, 2.41, 3.45 and 3.94 from Aug 2017 to Mar 2019, then 1.41 in Apr to Jul 2019.

findings.heading: What held the account back before I took over
findings.intro: I first worked on the account under my manager's plan. These figures cover all 465 tweets from Jul 2014 to Jul 2017.

cards.title: of tweets were Instagram auto-shares
cards.text: That's 167 of the 465 tweets. On Twitter they showed as a bare link with no image and earned about a third of what a native image did.

cards.title: tweets a month, on and off
cards.text: Across 37 months, the busiest had 27 tweets and three had none at all, so followers had no reason to expect us.

cards.title: engagements per sales tweet
cards.text: That's the average across 110 discount tweets linking to the shop. The 84 tweets from events, like the London Triathlon, averaged 2.60.

changes.heading: What I changed when I took over social
changes.intro: Each row compares the 465 tweets before I led social with the 395 in my time leading it.

monthly.heading: Engagement reached 142 a month, more than double any month before
monthly.intro: Before I led social, no month passed 68 engagements.
monthly.title: Engagement per month, Jul 2014 to Jul 2019
monthly.alt: Monthly engagement for @triuk. Before I led social, no month passed 68. In my time it peaked at 142 in Dec 2018 and 137 in Jan 2019.
monthly.note: The peak came in Dec 2018, when the first Cervélo S5 Ultegra and 2019 Focus bikes arrived.

tweets.heading: The six best-performing tweets
tweets.intro: I've recreated each tweet here with its original text, date and counts.
tweets.author: TRI UK

items.text: We just had the first of many @cervelo S5 Ultegra spec bikes delivered! This beautiful blue S5 is unlike any S5 Cervelo have released before. Super lightweight, aero, comfortable and at a great price point. What more could you want from a bike ? #cervelo #s5 #road #ride

This limited-edition speed machine unites brands that are both deeply committed to cutting-edge engineering, R&D, and raising the bar with every new product.

@cervelo and @Lamborghini join Forces on this fantastic Limited-Edition P5X.
Check out this beauty of a @cervelo P5 leaving our Yeovil store today! Fully kitted out with a set of @ZippSpeed wheels, this is sure to be one of the fastest bikes around 🔥

Here it is, the brand new for 2019 @FOCUSBikes Izalco Max 8.7! Focus have totally re-designed the #izalcomax to create a faster and lighter frame as well as incorporating discs into the range. With a carbon wheelset and priced at only £2649, this bike is sure to be a top seller.

This @cervelo R5 classics edition has been treated to a gold service from our workshop team. It’s also kitted up with a new @kmcchain to match the @fabriccycling bar tape, to finish of the build, a top quality set of @Mavic Comete UST wheels! One of our favourite builds for sure!

Seems like Santa has popped by early and delivered 90 @cervelo bikes! 🎅 

Including the new 2019 #Cervelo #S3 & #S5 for those riders who crave road-blurring speed.

lessons.heading: What TRI UK taught me about social

items.title: Post natively
items.text: Cross-posted links earned about 70% less than images uploaded straight to Twitter.

items.title: Tag the brand
items.text: Every one of the top six tweets tagged the bike brand.

items.title: Show the store and workshop
items.text: Store and workshop tweets earned nearly twice what discount tweets did.

items.title: Keep a steady rhythm
items.text: From Oct 2017 to Mar 2019 I tweeted at least 10 times every month.

items.title: Plan around launches
items.text: New-range deliveries and race weekends produced every peak in five years.

lessons.note: About the data: every public tweet from @triuk between Jul 2014 and Jul 2019, 1,150 in all. Engagement means likes, retweets and replies on TRI UK's own tweets, so treat the figures as a guide rather than exact.
